newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel provident fund redemptions up in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Israel provident fund redemptions up in Sept.

text.p: Net public redemptions from provident funds in September totalled 3.511 billion shekels, against net withdrawals of 2.241 billion shekels in August, Israel's Treasury said on Tuesday.
In July net redemptions totalled 943 million shekels.
The Treasury figures are based on orders given to the five biggest banks on August 13 for September.
According to initial bank estimates, there has been a significant decrease in redemptions in October, the Treasury said.
Since the beginning of the year net public redemptions from provident funds totalled 10.887 billion shekels.
The Treasury said bank figures show that a large portion of the money redeemed was deposited in savings accounts.

Net deposits in savings accounts in September totalled 1.937 billion shekels against 1.475 billion shekels in August. In the first nine months of the year, net deposits in saving plans totalled 5.169 billion shekels.
Provident funds, long term savings funds with tax benefits, have been faced with a wave of public redemptions triggered off by their poor performance in the past year.
